hook_line: Same customer every night. Same prescription. Same lie.

beats.visual: Dot smiles through the glass; Ivy hands over the bag.
beats.vo: Mrs Ferris. Sleeping tablets for her husband.

originality_review: Original. A caregiver who sedates an entity in her late husband's place is our own premise and expresses the brand tagline directly. It avoids MW006 (sleep study) and widow-ghost tropes, since the 'husband' is never a ghost.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Every night an elderly neighbour collects sleeping tablets for a husband who died nine years ago. When she finally misses a night, the one she kept asleep comes to the hatch himself.

hooks.line: Same customer every night. Same prescription. Same lie.
hooks.first_visual: A pharmacy hatch at 2 a.m.; a teal-cardigan elbow; a paper bag slid under the glass.

hooks.line: Her husband died nine years ago. She still collects his pills.
hooks.first_visual: A pharmacy screen showing a record, a date highlighted.

hooks.line: Who was she really buying sleeping tablets for?
hooks.first_visual: An old woman's hand clutching a small paper bag to her chest.

hooks.line: Tonight she didn't come. Then the bell rang.
hooks.first_visual: An empty hatch, a clock passing 3:00.

hooks.line: Some things should stay asleep. She made sure of it.
hooks.first_visual: A very tall figure in a too-small teal cardigan beyond the glass.

setting: Night pharmacy hatch at 2-3 a.m.; glass, slot, bell, shelves glowing behind Ivy.
conflict: Ivy suspects Dot is confused or stockpiling and wonders whether to stop serving her.
escalation: Dot grows frailer each night; then a night with no Dot.
reveal: A towering figure in Dot's cardigan: 'My wife is sleeping now.'
emotional_objective: Melancholy that turns to dread; the tagline made literal.
visual_requirements: Tenant in the same cardigan, too small
